skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

version.changelog:
- Evidence and demand signals updated from 12 to 10 across all documentation.
- References to skill-card.md have been removed.
- All README and SKILL files revised for consistency with the latest requirement plan.
- No changes to core functionality or workflow; only documentation and evidence updates.

llm.summary: The skill is documentation-only and not destructive, but its very broad implicit activation could pull it into unrelated conversations.

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown and YAML only, with no commands, dependencies, network retrieval, credential handling, local indexing, or data mutation instructions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install scripts or executable files were found; the only integration metadata inspected is a small agents/openai.yaml file with a default prompt and implicit invocation enabled.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill and README use broad trigger terms such as security, gate, every, must, pass, before, and activate, and the OpenAI agent policy allows implicit invocation, making accidental activation plausible outside the stated SkillScan workflow purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanisms, memory-writing instructions, background workers, privilege escalation, auth/session access, or tool replacement behavior were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a general workflow helper for SkillScan-style security, hardening, reliability, checklists, analysis, and implementation support; the artifacts do not request special runtime capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you use automatic skill routing. It is safest when invoked explicitly for SkillScan-style workflow help; broad implicit triggers like security, every, must, before, and activate should be narrowed or disabled to avoid unrelated conversations being routed through this skill.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] unexpected: Verified from SKILL.md, README files, the Chinese variants, requirement-plan.md, and agents/openai.yaml: the broad trigger vocabulary and implicit invocation are real scope concerns, but they are not evidence of malicious behavior because the package is non-executable and contains no hidden data access, persistence, or destructive instructions.
